message.content:
When people think of the “best” jazz vocalist, opinions vary, but a few names consistently rise to the top:

| Singer | Why they’re often called the best |
|--------|-----------------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑sing mastery, and effortless phrasing set a standard for jazz vocalists. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her deeply emotive delivery and unique phrasing turned standards into personal statements; she’s a benchmark for emotional depth. |
| **Sarah Sullivan** | A contemporary icon whose powerful voice and modern interpretations keep her at the forefront of jazz today. |
| **Louis Armstrong** | Though primarily a trumpeter, his gravelly, charismatic singing style helped popularize jazz worldwide. |
| **Nat King Cole** | His smooth baritone and crossover appeal made him a bridge between jazz, pop, and R&B. |

If you’re looking for a single “best” name, many would point to **Ella Fitzgerald** because of her technical perfection, versatility, and lasting influence on all subsequent jazz singers. However, the beauty of jazz is that it thrives on individuality—so the “best” can be as much about personal taste as about technical skill.
